scope: Sectional review of masking, retention/removal, shared evidence and sealed-key boundaries. Detailed authentication, all derived multi-key cases, network policy and backup restore remain outside this review.

additional_requirements.heading: Privacy
additional_requirements.statement: Create the archive directory 0700 and its files 0600 regardless of umask; status warns about wider permissions.
additional_requirements.why_distinct: Masking and listener-token laws do not independently specify local archive filesystem permissions.

additional_requirements.heading: Purge: the one true deletion
additional_requirements.statement: General purge is operator-initiated from an interactive terminal, never automatic or available to agents/MCP; backed excision uses its distinct declared pathway.
additional_requirements.why_distinct: Dry-run/shared-byte and compressed-DML laws do not identify who may initiate irreversible purge.

additional_requirements.heading: The design: three confidentiality classes on one mechanism (2026-10-11)
additional_requirements.statement: Sealed names and deltas respect data-key boundaries; destroying one key does not destroy separately keyed content, and locked reads/replay do not expose sealed plaintext.
additional_requirements.why_distinct: Capture redaction and output masking laws do not establish cryptographic material-key isolation or locked replay behavior.

additional_requirements.heading: The design: three confidentiality classes on one mechanism (2026-10-11)
additional_requirements.statement: Exclude the wrapped data-key table from long-term database backups; its separately retained backups can still unlock shredded data until their stated retention window expires.
additional_requirements.why_distinct: Live-store purge and shared-byte laws do not establish when older backups stop retaining decryptable keys.

additional_requirements.heading: Purge: the one true deletion
additional_requirements.statement: Before physical completion, repoint/re-encode retained extents and delta/revision dependencies needing only surviving bytes; outside-scope overlaps block completion until the operator explicitly expands the exact scope.
additional_requirements.why_distinct: Shared-byte survival and dry-run laws do not independently require removal of purged bytes from retained backing dependencies or define overlapping-scope refusal.

additional_requirements.heading: Purge: the one true deletion
additional_requirements.statement: Purge prior derived payloads and archived bodies that depend on removed parents; recompute from surviving parents as a new replacement without retaining the old mixed-parent content.
additional_requirements.why_distinct: Provenance and read-model laws do not independently distinguish ordinary archival from removal of historical mixed-parent payloads during purge.

obligations.heading: Privacy
obligations.acceptance: Use synthetic credentials through CLI/MCP/export/HTTP response encoding; reveal is refused outside an operator terminal or with a harness, and default output is masked.

obligations.heading: The design: three confidentiality classes on one mechanism (2026-10-11)
obligations.acceptance: Exercise private capture and admission redaction plus guarded/sealed output grants; plaintext material is not called protected merely because event fields are masked.

obligations.heading: Inputs, revisions and extents
obligations.acceptance: Provider deletion and lossy rewrites preserve prior acquired evidence; hiding a session does not excise it or delete its originals.

obligations.heading: 7. Retention, deletion and archive
obligations.acceptance: Separate removed-at-source, excluded, retracted and purged cases; archive/replay keeps original evidence and no original expires by age.

obligations.heading: How excision works
obligations.acceptance: An isolated synthetic excision is previewed and confirmed by the permitted operator route; agents cannot invoke it as an ordinary write.

obligations.heading: Purge: the one true deletion
obligations.acceptance: Use the operator-only synthetic purge route with dry-run parity; exclusion undo does not undo purge, and compression changes remain scoped.

obligations.heading: How excision works
obligations.acceptance: Excise one session in a shared input, including delta bases and archive members; unaffected bytes/structure remain readable with valid references.

obligations.heading: Purge: the one true deletion
obligations.acceptance: Purge a selected range with outside-scope extents and delta bases needing only surviving bytes: all old backing dependencies are safely replaced and deleted. A genuine overlapping outside-scope reference blocks completion and is named, without silently widening scope.

obligations.heading: Privacy
obligations.acceptance: Create state under a permissive umask and inspect archive/file modes and warnings; default local plaintext is not described as encryption at rest.

obligations.heading: The design: three confidentiality classes on one mechanism (2026-10-11)
obligations.acceptance: Seal equal plaintext under independent keys, refuse cross-key deltas, lock and defer reads/replay; shred one key and demonstrate the old wrapped-key backup caveat without claiming immediate backup erasure.

obligations.heading: Deletion (joint #6)
obligations.acceptance: Exclude local content immediately; backed tombstones/privacy completion remain separately pending until confirmed, while shared replacements and content-free frontier bookkeeping survive.

obligations.heading: Purge: the one true deletion
obligations.acceptance: Purge one parent of a mixed-parent result already archived/cached: old derived payloads disappear, survivors produce new replacements, and a fresh content-free change invalidates historical caches before broker cleanup.

obligations.heading: How excision works
obligations.acceptance: Grow/re-import an excised input and union an older archive; standing hashes/scopes prevent forbidden content from returning without deleting unrelated shared inputs.

obligations.heading: 7. Retention, deletion and archive
obligations.acceptance: Replay/re-import purged or excluded occurrences with stable keys; undo restores only undoable exclusion, never purged bytes or keys.

obligations.heading: How excision works
obligations.acceptance: Kill between rewritten-blob, extent, index, vector and backed-confirmation boundaries; resume cleanup and inspect immediate read exclusion separately from pending physical work.

obligations.heading: Purge: the one true deletion
obligations.acceptance: Crash around purge commit/file removal/stream cleanup, then retry; no removed payload is served or republished, and unaffected shared content survives.
